{{Short description|Endowed professorship at Harvard College}}
The '''Hollis Chair of Mathematicks and Natural Philosophy''' {{sic}} is an [[Financial endowment|endowed]] [[professor]]ship established at [[Harvard College]] in 1727 by [[Thomas Hollis (1659–1731)|Thomas Hollis]].<ref name=Quin1915>{{Cite book |title=Quinquennial catalogue of the officers and graduates of Harvard university, 1636–1915 |year=1915 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge, MA |page=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_JiNOAAAAMAAJ/page/n478 21] |url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_JiNOAAAAMAAJ |access-date=2011-04-17 }}</ref> The chair, now part of the Physics Department, is the second oldest at Harvard, and the oldest professorship in science in the United States.

The spelling of the title of the chair has been retained since its establishment.<ref>[https://hetg.physics.harvard.edu/news/professor-cumrun-vafa-appointed-hollis-professor-mathematicks-and-natural-philosophy Appointment to Hollis Professorship 9 July 2018]</ref> The original Rules and Orders relating to the chair are still extant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iiif.lib.harvard.edu/manifests/view/drs:50969000|title = Harvard Mirador Viewer}}</ref>

The incumbents have been:
* [[Isaac Greenwood]] (1727–1737)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[John Winthrop (educator)|John Winthrop]] (1737–1779)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[Samuel Williams (minister)|Samuel Williams]] (1779–1789)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[Samuel Webber]] (1789–1806)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[John Farrar (scientist)|John Farrar]] (1807–1838)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[Joseph Lovering]] (1838–1888)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[Benjamin Osgood Peirce]] (1888–1914)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* [[Wallace Clement Sabine]] (1914–1919)<ref name=Quin1915/>
* vacant (January 1919–September 1921)<ref>{{cite journal|title=Faculty Appointments|journal=Harvard Alumni Bulletin|date=September 29, 1921|volume=24|issue=1|page=40|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UTY6AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA40}} Sabine died in January 1919, and Lyman was not appointed until September 1921.</ref>
* [[Theodore Lyman IV|Theodore Lyman]] (1921–1926)
* [[Percy Williams Bridgman]] (1926–1950)
* [[John Hasbrouck Van Vleck]] (1951–1969)
* [[Andrew Gleason]] (1969–1992)
* [[Bertrand Halperin]] (1992–2018)
* [[Cumrun Vafa]] (2018–2026)
* [[Laura DeMarco]] (2026–present)<ref>{{cite web|title=Laura DeMarco Appointed Hollis Professor of Mathematicks and Natural Philosophy|url=https://www.math.harvard.edu/laura-demarco-appointed-hollis-professor-of-mathematicks-and-natural-philosophy/}} </ref>
